title: A Quiet Word About Unintentional Plagiarism
script: Professor Wibowo: [thoughtful] Larasati, I need to talk to you about your essay. Several paragraphs closely mirror a source that isn't cited anywhere in your bibliography.
Larasati: What? I promise I didn't copy anything deliberately, I must have paraphrased too closely without realizing it.
Professor Wibowo: [carefully] I believe you, actually, which is precisely why I wanted to speak with you privately rather than report it immediately.
Larasati: Thank you for that. I genuinely thought I'd reworded those sections enough.
Professor Wibowo: [reflective] That's a common mistake, changing a few words while keeping the original sentence structure intact, which technically still counts as plagiarism, even unintentionally.
Larasati: Does intention matter at all here, or am I going to be treated the same as someone who copied on purpose?
Professor Wibowo: [honestly] Intention matters enormously to me, though I won't pretend every colleague would draw that same distinction.
Professor Wibowo: [gently] You'll revise those paragraphs and resubmit by Friday, properly cited this time, and I'll adjust your grade rather than fail the assignment outright.
Larasati: That's far more understanding than I expected, honestly.
Professor Wibowo: [calmly] Don't mistake understanding for indifference, though. If this happens again, I won't be able to justify the same leniency to the department.
Larasati: It won't happen again. I'll start using citation software instead of trusting my memory of what I've paraphrased.
Professor Wibowo: [encouraging] That's a sensible habit to build now, before the stakes get considerably higher in graduate work.
Larasati: Can I ask something? How do you usually tell the difference between carelessness and someone who's genuinely trying to deceive you?
Professor Wibowo: [seriously] Mostly by what happens after I raise it. Panic and a willingness to fix things honestly usually look quite different from excuses.
Larasati: Well, I suppose panic was exactly what you got from me a few minutes ago.
Professor Wibowo: It was, and it told me everything I needed to know.
